comparison: Perfect agreement on C29-C34. Both evaluations find the CRISPR knockout approach robust and the CFU data convincing. OpenEval notes appropriate controls and consistency with literature; peer reviewers affirm methodological strength and convincing data.

Perfect agreement on C39-C45. Both evaluations support the Seahorse metabolic flux analysis data. OpenEval details technical replicates and statistical comparisons; peer reviewers explicitly praise metabolic assays as strengthening the study.

Perfect agreement on C50-C54. Both evaluations support the HIF1α and pAMPK western blot findings. OpenEval notes statistical significance but suggests loading control improvements; peer reviewers accept the signaling pathway findings without question.

Strong disagreement on C57-C59. OpenEval finds autophagy claims supported but notes LC3 data alone is ambiguous and recommends flux assays. Peer Reviewer 3 rates evidence as UNCERTAIN, stating LC3 western blot is unconvincing without BafA1/chloroquine controls and evidence is incomplete.

Perfect agreement on C68-C73. Both evaluations support the rescue experiments with Mtb Δicl1 and fatty acid supplementation. OpenEval finds the lipid droplet paradox particularly compelling; peer reviewers note rescue experiments strengthen reliability.

Perfect agreement on C112-C115. Both evaluations support the chemical inhibitor data showing host-mediated effects. OpenEval emphasizes validation of genetic knockouts and therapeutic potential; peer reviewers accept HDT implications without question.

Agreement on C35-C36. Both evaluations support the lipid droplet findings and accept the discrepancy with Knight et al. 2018. OpenEval provides mechanistic explanation for the contradiction; Peer Reviewer 4 notes this challenges previous assumptions.

Agreement on C74-C78 (RNA-seq quality and differential expression). OpenEval supports the data but requests clarification on replicates and batch effects; peer reviewers praise the transcriptomic approach as providing deep insights without raising concerns.

Agreement on C79-C82, C91 (Slc27a1-/- pro-inflammatory signature and compensatory transporters). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval notes consistency with literature and plausible mechanistic explanation; peer reviewers accept transcriptomic findings without question.

Agreement on C84-C88, C92 (Plin2-/- and Cpt2-/- anti-inflammatory phenotypes). Both evaluations support these pathway enrichment findings. OpenEval notes contrast with Slc27a1-/- suggesting distinct mechanisms; peer reviewers accept as part of comprehensive transcriptomic analysis.

Agreement on C89-C90 (Cd36-/- pathway enrichment). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval notes similarity to Plin2-/- but questions whether small gene number reflects subtle response or power issues; peer reviewers accept without concern.

Agreement on C93-C96 (bacterial RNA-seq findings). Both evaluations support the bacterial transcriptome data. OpenEval finds lack of differential expression in Slc27a1-/- surprising but consistent with compensatory mechanisms; peer reviewers praise dual RNA-seq approach.

Agreement on C97-C105 (bacterial metabolic gene upregulation indicating nutrient limitation). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval notes interpretation is reasonable but acknowledges alternative explanations; peer reviewers accept bacterial transcriptome evidence for nutrient limitation mechanism.

Agreement on C106-C108, C110 (bacterial oxidative stress response genes). Both evaluations support bacterial transcriptomic evidence of oxidative stress. OpenEval finds FurA downregulation specific and well-characterized; peer reviewers accept as part of dual RNA-seq findings.

Partial disagreement on C111 (host ROS measurements). OpenEval finds CellROX staining provides direct evidence of elevated ROS and rates as SUPPORTED. Peer Reviewer 3 rates as UNCERTAIN, requesting representative images with Mtb co-staining for clarity on infected cells.

Disagreement on C3 (integrative conclusion about common mechanisms). OpenEval finds the main conclusion well-supported by collective evidence including glycolysis, oxidative stress, and autophagy. Peer Reviewer 3 rates as UNCERTAIN, stating evidence for glycolysis and cytokines is strong but autophagy and oxidative stress evidence is incomplete.

Agreement on C36 (discrepancy with Knight et al. 2018). Both evaluations accept this finding. OpenEval provides detailed explanation about germline vs. acute myeloid-specific deletion; peer reviewers note it challenges previous assumptions without questioning the interpretation.

Agreement on C109 (bacterial transcriptional similarity between Plin2-/- and Cpt2-/-). Both evaluations support this finding. OpenEval notes consistency with host transcriptional similarity but questions statistical power with only 10 genes; peer reviewers accept as part of bacterial RNA-seq analysis.

OpenEval evaluated C118 (upregulation of alternative lipid transporters in Slc27a1-/-) as SUPPORTED, noting this compensatory mechanism explains moderate Mtb restriction. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim.
